title: UK Consumer Confidence Jumps Amidst Speculation of New PM
summary: Consumer confidence in the UK increased by its largest margin in nearly three years due to speculation about a potential new prime minister. The data company GfK reported a 'wave of optimism' sparked by the prospect of Andy Burnham becoming prime minister, alongside England's football team progress and hot weather. This month's consumer confidence jumped 3.4 percentage points, exceeding expectations. The UK's Consumer Confidence Index rose to 104.8 in July, surpassing its previous peak in 2019. GfK attributed the surge to a combination of factors, including improved economic prospects and a sense of national pride following England's World Cup success.
summary_points: Consumer confidence in the UK increased by 3.4 percentage points this month
The increase was attributed to speculation about Andy Burnham becoming prime minister
England's football team progress and hot weather also contributed to the surge
This month's Consumer Confidence Index rose to 104.8, surpassing its previous peak in 2019
